newsitem.title: USA: First Union sees fee income rising 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: First Union sees fee income rising 20 pct.

text.p: First Union Corp chief financial officer Robert Atwood told reporters in a telephone conference call Thursday that he expects fee income to rise 20 percent in 1997 and net interest income to rise five percent.
"We're looking at 20 percent or better growth," Atwood said of the fee income outlook in response to a question.

Chief credit officer Mal Murray said the credit card chargeoff rate declined to 5.75 percent in the fourth quarter from 5.9 percent in the third quarter. He said the decline reflected an increase in outstanding credit card loans to about $7.0 billion from $6.7 billion.
Credit card loans at Charlotte, N.C.-based First Union account for about six percent of the total loan portfolio.
Murray said First Union believes credit cards are an integral and necessary part ot its business and the company has no intention of withdrawing from card lending.
First Union said in its fourth-quarter earnings release that for all of 1996, capital management fee income increased 32 percent and capital markets fee income increased 78 percent to $479 million.
Operating earnings for 1996 rose 19 percent to $1.76 billion, or $6.31 per share.

Atwood said First Union's mutual fund business doubled in size with the acquistion of Keystone Investments, which was completed on December 11. The mutual funds totaled $27.1 billion at the end of the year.
Referring to capital markets products, Atwood said First Union is seeing very strong demand for products from middle market business customers up and down the U.S. East Coast.
The capital markets business includes risk management products, loan syndication and investment banking services.
